docstring:
Let $0 < \epsilon < 1$. Is it true that, if $k$ is sufficiently large, then
$$R(G) > (1-\epsilon)^k R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

The restriction $\epsilon < 1$ excludes negative bases in $(1-\epsilon)^k$.

This problem is #12 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
references: [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ε < 1 →
    ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        G.chromaticNumber = ↑k → ↑G.diagonalGraphRamsey > (1 - ε) ^ k * ↑(SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k)
